subject: Urgent: v12q P95 latency surge — intervention gate request
messages:
From: Allen Park <allen@finlytics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+infra@finlytics.com
Date: 2028-09-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: P95 jump after v12q rollout — need rapid coordination

Hi Kimberly / Markus,

We started seeing a sustained P95 latency spike on text-generation calls originating from our Prod cluster about 07:30 UTC, right after v12q was promoted yesterday. Baseline P95 was ~210ms; over the last 90m we've seen bursts to 1.3s for medium-length prompts (tokens 64-256). Error rates are unchanged, but tail latency is severely impacting UX.

Quick facts:
- Model: v12q (serving variant v12q-2028-09-11-rc3)
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (customer route: finlytics-prod)
- Observed: 210ms -> 1.3s p95 (sustained); p99 spikes to ~2.8s
- Recent change: quantization kernel update + auto-batching policy change on 09/11 rollout

Can Redwood perform an emergency intervention? We need one of the following ASAP: a temporary traffic throttle to reduce concurrency, a canary rollback to v12p, or an emergency hotpatch to the batching kernel. Please advise on risk and ETA.

Attaching a small packet of representative traces and SLO-extract (finlytics-p95-sample-logs.zip).

Thanks,
Allen
Director, Platform Reliability
Finlytics
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Allen Park <allen@finlytics.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ev evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-12T09:29:00Z
Subject: Re: P95 jump after v12q rollout — need rapid coordination

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs, Allen.

We’ve triaged preliminarily and see an increased queueing delay inside the batching codepath for sequences between ~80–220 tokens. Initial hypothesis: a kernel selection regression in the v12q quantized path combined with the new batching policy.

Proposed emergency measures (pick one):
- Temporary per-customer concurrency cap (throttle finlytics-prod to target 60% of current burst concurrency) — low-risk, immediate, preserves throughput but increases tail queuing slightly.
- Canary rollback for the finlytics route to v12p (compatible model variant) — medium-risk for quality drift but fastest to restore p95.
- Hotpatch deploying patched batching kernel to the affected fleet subset (requires SRE runbook and 30–45min convo window).

Requesting authorization from Markus (engineering change) and Evelyn (CS customer communications) to proceed with chosen path. If no objections, I recommend starting with the per-customer concurrency cap + scheduled canary rollback if issues persist.

Notes: I’ve attached the SLO extract you provided to this thread and uploaded the runbook momentarily to our ops links.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Allen Park <allen@finlytics.com>, ev evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-12T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: P95 jump after v12q rollout — need rapid coordination

Kimberly — thanks for the breakdown. I approve immediate activation of the per-customer concurrency cap for finlytics-prod (target 60% of their current peak). Rationale: minimal blast radius, buys time to validate.

Action items for SRE (assigning to oncall):
- Apply throttle policy to route finlytics-prod (ETA 5–10 mins).
- Run short traffic-generating canary to compare v12q vs v12p (10–15 mins).
- If canary shows restored p95 on v12p, coordinate a route-level rollback (canary -> rollback) and prep release notes for CS.

Risks:
- If quality delta between v12p and v12q is meaningful for Finlytics workload, CS must clear rollback with the customer.
- Hotpatch is heavier lift and needs a maintenance window authorization.

I’ll stand by on the runbook link: https://app.redwood.ai/runbooks/v12q-hotpatch — SRE lead should follow section 3 for throttle + canary steps.

—Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Serving Runtime
From: ev evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Allen Park <allen@finlytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-12T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: P95 jump after v12q rollout — need rapid coordination

Allen — we appreciate the escalation. From a customer-facing perspective, a short concurrency cap with clear comms is preferable to an immediate rollback; it reduces risk of quality regressions. If we proceed with rollback we need a quick A/B summary to show the expected difference in token-level accuracy/QA signals.

Customer ask: can Redwood promise a temporary SLA tolerance window (P95 allowance up to 1.5s) during the containment window while we execute canary rollback? Finlytics will need that for internal incident reports.

Proposed customer-facing statement (draft):
"We’re implementing a temporary traffic containment to stabilize tail latency while we validate a rollback option. We expect minimal functional impact; we will update you with the result of a short A/B canary within 45 minutes."

If Finlytics signs off to the draft we can proceed.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Allen Park <allen@finlytics.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ev evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, ops+infra@finlytics.com
Date: 2028-09-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: P95 jump after v12q rollout — intervention gate request (decision)

Allen — thank you. Per approvals from engineering and CS, we are executing the following now: 

1) Immediate: apply per-route concurrency cap for finlytics-prod to 60% of peak (SRE oncall executing). ETA ~10 minutes.
2) Next: run A/B canary comparing v12q -> v12p on a small traffic slice (10–15 minutes).
3) If canary restores P95 without unacceptable quality delta, we will roll the route back to v12p and notify you.

We have agreed to a provisional SLA tolerance statement as Evelyn drafted — Finlytics may use it for internal reporting. If you need this as a signed exception, let us know and we can route to legal for a short-term SLA carveout.

Links: runbook (https://app.redwood.ai/runbooks/v12q-hotpatch), HubSpot record (https://hubspot.company/contacts/FIN-2028-0421). Attachments include the logs you sent (finlytics-p95-sample-logs.zip) and the SLO extract we pulled for the window.

I’ll follow up once the canary completes.

Best,
Kimberly
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: finlytics-p95-sample-logs.zip, slo-extract-20280912.csv
